editorNote: A quiet day for the watchlist's operating businesses but a loud one for two of its macro proxies: bitcoin broke back above $80,000 on a short squeeze and fresh Treasury buyback plans, and gold pushed to a three-month high on dollar weakness. Alibaba's steep discount sends its shares lower even as its top executives stepped in to buy the dip.

stories.headline: Alibaba's top executives buy $15 million in shares after its discounted $10.2 billion AI share sale
stories.summary: Alibaba sold 710 million new shares at HK$112.70 each, an 8.4% discount to Friday's close, to raise HK$80 billion ($10.2 billion) for AI infrastructure; Hong Kong shares fell as much as 10.5% before paring losses, even as the offering drew about $28 billion in orders. Chairman Joseph Tsai and CEO Eddie Wu then bought roughly HK$120 million ($15.3 million) of stock on the open market.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the largest-ever follow-on share sale by a Hong Kong-listed company, and the insider buying signals executives view the AI-funding dilution as worth the near-term stock hit.

sourceLinks.title: Alibaba shares slide after $10.2 billion AI share sale offered at sharp discount

stories.headline: Bitcoin tops $80,000 for the first time since May on a short squeeze
stories.summary: Bitcoin rose more than 2% to around $80,500, its highest since May, extending a rally that saw it jump over 20% in three days last week -- its biggest three-day gain since 2023. The move was fueled by a short squeeze that liquidated more than $4 billion in bearish positions, alongside the U.S. Treasury's announcement it will increase purchases of longer-dated bonds and strong inflows into bitcoin and ether ETFs.
stories.whyItMatters: The breakout follows a prolonged slump since October, and analysts note a similar January 2023 surge initially faded, leaving the rally's durability untested.

sourceLinks.title: Bitcoin surges past $80,000 as crypto rally gathers pace

stories.headline: Gold hits highest level since mid-May as the dollar weakens
stories.summary: Spot gold rose 0.6% to $4,677.19 an ounce, its highest since mid-May, while futures gained 0.5% to $4,720.30. Gold has climbed more than 15% this month, which UOB forecasts as its strongest monthly gain since September 1999, driven by U.S. dollar weakness and the Treasury's bond buyback plans.
stories.whyItMatters: The rally remains well below the roughly $5,600 record set earlier this year, underscoring how sharply gold has round-tripped in 2026.

sourceLinks.title: Gold hits over three-month high on dollar weakness, Treasury bond buyback plans
